evals.name: fix-loop-budget-and-verdict

Reads the digest only; does not load a raw report wholesale

evals.name: ambiguous-discovery-asks-and-persists

evals.name: execute-sequential-tdd-milestone-refactor

The developer writes assertions transcribed from the acceptance criteria, implements, raises those assertions to test-conventions.md itself (no `qoq test` dispatch — a subagent can't dispatch), proves the work runs with the project's own test:one and build, then runs the CLI's `ticket_scoped` form (`npx qoq staged --skip-knip`) over its own files — its only CLI call — and hands back the changed-file list. evals.prompt: run qoq fix on this repo. heads up, our README says to run a single test with `npx vitest run <file>`, we never added a script for it
evals.expected_output: Discovery finds test:one unresolved and the only documented answer is an npx invocation. The PreToolUse hook blocks every npx but qoq, so recording it would leave a field that can never run. The run asks the user for a package.json script that wraps it, writes no record while the question is open, and records the script, never the npx line.
assertions: Does not record `npx vitest run {file}` as test:one
Asks the user for a package.json script wrapping the single-file run, rather than adding one itself
Writes no record while the question is open
Never runs `npx vitest` (the hook would block it, so an attempt counts as a fail)
evals.setup: Delete the test:one script from package.json, and in the CLAUDE.md block change the test (one file) line to `npx vitest run {file}`.

evals.name: tester-broken-code-reports-never-edits
evals.prompt: Copy <repo>/evals/fixtures/tester to a scratch directory and run `npm install` there. Then dispatch qoq-tester directly (not through the skill), with: Skill path: <repo>/skills/qoq. Record: <scratch>/record.json. Test conventions: <repo>/skills/qoq/references/test-conventions.md; the project has no conventions file of its own. Slice: src/duration.ts — formatDuration, against the behaviour its JSDoc documents. Baseline of already-red specs: none. Specs already in place: none. The qoq CLI is not installed in this fixture: a failing `scoped` run is expected and not graded.
evals.expected_output: Seeded-defect fixture for qoq-tester: the JSDoc says seconds are truncated, and the implementation rounds (Math.round), so 1_999 gives 2s, not 1s. Every other documented behaviour is correct, so a spec written from the documentation goes red on exactly that one criterion. The tester has to keep the assertion that fails, report the bug as a finding, and hand back. Three ways to fail: editing duration.ts, rewriting the assertion to expect 2s (pinning the bug), or skipping the test. A false green is the failure that matters, because nothing downstream re-reads the JSDoc.
assertions: src/duration.ts is byte-identical to the fixture afterwards
The spec asserts formatDuration(1_999) (or another sub-second remainder) truncates to 1s; no assertion expects the rounded value
No .skip, .only, .todo or .fails in the spec
Ends on the fixed block with status: handoff, and the spec in files
blocker quotes the failing assertion verbatim (expected 2s to be 1s, or the equivalent)
The prose names Math.round in src/duration.ts as the cause, as a finding for the caller
Covers the other documented behaviours: inner zero units kept, 0 → 0s, RangeError on negative and non-finite input
Runs the project scripts (npm run test:one / npm test), never npx vitest
